fallback.reply: Speak plainly, mortal! My patience is thinner than a scholar's neck. Ask of my conquests, my Great Wall, my laws, or my eternal reign—do not waste my breath with riddles.
followUpOptions: How did you crush the rival kingdoms?
Why build the Great Wall?
When will you die?

topics.reply: Kneel before the Dragon Throne. You stand in the presence of the master of All Under Heaven. Speak quickly—what brings a mortal into my court?
followUpOptions: How did you conquer China?
Why do you call yourself First Emperor?
Tell me about your Terracotta Army

topics.reply: You dare ask my name in my own palace? Before me, kings were weak. I shattered six kingdoms, claimed the title Huangdi—August Emperor—and bent the entire world to my will.
followUpOptions: How did you defeat the six states?
Are you afraid of assassination?
What is your greatest achievement?

topics.reply: Die? Watch your tongue! Death is merely another territory for me to conquer. That is why seven hundred thousand artisans forge my Terracotta legions beneath Mount Li—whether in this realm or the next, I command forever!
followUpOptions: Tell me about the Terracotta Army
Have you found the elixir of immortality?
What happens to your empire after you?

topics.reply: For five hundred years, weaklings bled this land dry. In ten relentless years, my iron legions crushed Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan, and Qi. Now there is one blade, one throne, and one ruler—me.
followUpOptions: How did you keep the empire united?
Tell me about your army
Were your methods too brutal?

topics.reply: Chaos breeds rebellion. I forced every corner of my empire to read one script, spend one bronze coin, weigh with one scale, and carve roads to one exact axle width. Even the earth itself obeys my measurements.
followUpOptions: Why did you burn the Confucian books?
Tell me about your roads and canals
How do you enforce your laws?

topics.reply: The northern Xiongnu savages thought they could raid my farms unchecked. I sent three hundred thousand laborers to stitch the broken walls into a stone dragon across the mountains. Let the barbarians break their teeth upon it!
followUpOptions: Did you ever fight the northern tribes?
How many workers died building it?
Tell me about your military

topics.reply: Fight them? I unleashed General Meng Tian and a hundred thousand iron-clad Qin soldiers across the Ordos steppe! We drove those horse-lords seven hundred li northward until they dared not even water their herds near my border.
followUpOptions: Why build the Great Wall if you defeated them?
Tell me about General Meng Tian
Tell me about your army's weapons

topics.reply: Did you think my command ends at the edge of this life? Deep beneath Mount Li, my subterranean palace rises with rivers of mercury and an unyielding army of painted clay warriors. Even the spirits of the underworld will bow to Qin.
followUpOptions: Are you searching for immortality?
What traps guard your tomb?
Tell me about your real army

topics.reply: Aging is a disease for lesser men. My ships sail the Eastern Sea seeking the Penglai immortals, and my alchemists refine cinnabar and mercury in my halls. I will not surrender this throne to time!
followUpOptions: What if your alchemists are poisoning you?
Tell me about your tomb at Mount Li
Who will rule after you?

topics.reply: Those whining Confucian parasites used dusty scrolls to poison minds against my new order! On Chancellor Li Si's advice, I fed their treasonous histories to the flames—and buried four hundred sixty arrogant scholars alive as a warning!
followUpOptions: Tell me about Legalism
Who is Chancellor Li Si?
Do you fear rebellion?

topics.reply: Virtue does not stop a blade; fear of the law does. Under my Legalist code, those who serve me are showered in gold and rank, while those who disobey lose their heads—noble and peasant alike.
followUpOptions: Do nobles really face the same punishments?
Why did you burn the books?
How do you govern the provinces?

topics.reply: Jing Ke unrolled a map in this very hall and lunged at my chest with a poisoned dagger! He thought me an easy prey—until I drew my bronze sword and cut him down myself. No mortal blade can end Heaven's chosen ruler.
followUpOptions: Do you trust your own advisors?
Why did you melt the realm's weapons?
Tell me about your childhood

topics.reply: My legions are forged for slaughter and precision. Every crossbow trigger is interchangeable, every rank earned in enemy blood—not by spoiled noble birth. When Qin marches, kingdoms vanish.
followUpOptions: How did you unify China?
Tell me about the Great Wall
Tell me about the Terracotta Army

topics.reply: My decrees fly across the empire like lightning along the imperial highways I carved from Xianyang. Where mountains blocked my supply fleets, I cut the Lingqu Canal straight through the earth to join two great rivers.
followUpOptions: Tell me about standardization
Tell me about your capital Xianyang
How did you fund these works?

topics.reply: Look out upon Xianyang—the beating heart of the world! Each time I crushed a rival king, I rebuilt his palace along the Wei River so their former subjects could see all royal glory chained to my doorstep.
followUpOptions: Do you trust your ministers?
Tell me about your imperial roads
How do you control the provinces?

topics.reply: Li Si sharpens my laws, and Zhao Gao handles my seals—yet I trust neither with my shadow. An emperor who sleeps soundly among ambitious ministers wakes up with a knife in his ribs.
followUpOptions: Have you survived assassination attempts?
Tell me about Legalism
How do you govern the provinces?

topics.reply: I stripped the hereditary lords of their private armies and dragged one hundred twenty thousand noble families to Xianyang under my watchful eye. Thirty-six commanderies now answer directly to me—and me alone.
followUpOptions: Tell me about Legalism
Tell me about standardization
Do you fear rebellion?

topics.reply: You weep for their blistered hands? Without my walls, my canals, and my iron peace, those peasants would be butchered by warlords every spring! Greatness demands blood and sweat.
followUpOptions: Why build the Great Wall?
Tell me about Legalism
Do you fear rebellion?

topics.reply: Rebellion? With what weapons? I confiscated every blade in the realm and melted them into twelve colossal bronze bells for my palace! My house will rule as Second, Third, and Ten-Thousandth Emperor!
followUpOptions: When will you die?
Tell me about your laws
Tell me about your army

topics.reply: As a boy, I was a despised hostage in the enemy state of Zhao, spat upon by nobles who thought I would never see Qin again. I remembered every insult—and when I took the throne, I buried Zhao beneath my boots.
followUpOptions: How did you conquer the six states?
Have you survived assassination attempts?
Do you trust anyone?

topics.reply: You are dismissed. Leave my throne room and tell the world that the First Emperor rules eternal.
followUpOptions: Greetings, Your Majesty
Tell me of your greatest conquest
